trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.summary: The platinum: it lands on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, in single player, with no multiplayer or DLC involved [1][2].
steps: Confirm the shape of the job first: 55 trophies, 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, every one of them offline [1][4].
Play one full playthrough — the roadmap sources agree a single run is enough, with free-roam after the story and no mission replay or New Game+ to lean on [1][3].
Protect the one risky trophy early: the Chapter 1 balcony meditation behind Positive Mental Attitude, flagged in the Missables view [1][7].
Keep cheats off for the whole run, because the guides agree cheats disable trophies and saving [1][7].
Work the tracker stage by stage; when the earned count reads 54 of 55 with only this one open, finish any last trophy and the platinum follows automatically [2][6].
Re-check the Missables view before every chapter ends; it is the one screen that can save the whole run [1][3].

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.summary: A story trophy for finishing Gone Fishing, the opening main mission of Chapter 1; it unlocks by itself and cannot be missed [1][7].
steps: Start a new game and play the opening of Chapter 1, where Gone Fishing is the first main mission [1].
Follow the mission markers to the end of Gone Fishing; there are no optional objectives or medal targets attached to it [1].
Let the mission complete fully — the trophy is automatic on completion, not on any choice inside the mission [1][2].
Check the tracker afterwards: this is the first of the 12 hidden story trophies, so it stays masked on PlayStation until it pops [4][5].
Keep a manual save at the start of Chapter 1 anyway; with no mission replay in the game, chapter-start saves are your only safety net [1][3].
While the chapter is open, scan new vehicles with WAiNK and study animals through binoculars — both habits pay into the 100% checklist later [1].

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.summary: The Chapter 1 completion trophy; the guide places its unlock as the story rolls into Chapter 2, and it cannot be missed [1].
steps: Play through Chapter 1's main missions in order, starting with Gone Fishing [1][7].
Before you close the chapter, do the Chapter 1 balcony meditation at Jason's house (see Positive Mental Attitude) — it is gone once this chapter ends [1][3].

Scan vehicles with WAiNK and study animals through binoculars as you travel — 200 vehicle scans and 100 animal studies are checklist targets, and progress counts even before that checklist is visible [1].
Finish the chapter's last beats and move into Chapter 2's opening mission, What's in the Bag?, at which point this trophy unlocks [1].
Make your chapter-end manual save now, in a separate slot from the chapter-start one [1][3].

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

steps: Enter Chapter 2 through its opening mission, What's in the Bag? [1].
Play the chapter's main missions, including Breakfast Run (its own trophy, Trust) [1][7].
Use this chapter to unlock playing as both characters together — Coffee Break opens partner play, which several later trophies need [1].
Finish the chapter and start Chapter 3's opener, Welcome to Vice City, which is when the guide places this unlock [1].
Save manually at the chapter boundary, start and end, as the roadmap advises for every chapter [1][3].
Chapter 2 also installs the tools later trophies lean on: partner play opens here, and the garage and vehicle-registration systems arrive in this chapter [1].

Play the final mission to its end — completion, not performance, is what the trophy checks [1].

Do not spend the post-story freedom at random: open the checklist first and let its categories order your cleanup [1][8].

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.summary: The second gold and the hardest trophy in the set: finish the 100% Completion checklist, which opens after the story — and which the guides stress is far more lenient than true 100% [1][8].
steps: Finish the story first; the checklist lives under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion, and only appears after the credits [1][8].
Do not restart anything: progress you made during the story already counts toward the checklist [1][3].
Work the lenient thresholds — for example 200 of 277 base-model vehicles scanned, 100 of 255 animals studied, 70 of 80 challenges, 15 of 18 meditations [1][4].
Clear the categories that demand everything: robberies, underwater discoveries, shooting ranges, drone races and Bret's quests [1].
Take optional missions as they appear during the story; any 100 of them feed the checklist and there are far more than needed [1].
When the checklist reads complete, the gold unlocks — the sources put this stage at roughly 100 hours of the run [1][3].
If a category stalls, re-read its tracker page under Progress before grinding — several categories cap below their full pools [1].

disagree.b: Push Square's roadmap warns to set aside 250 to 300 hours or more for the platinum [8].
disagree.safe: Plan your time on the longer estimate and treat anything faster as a bonus; the checklist thresholds themselves agree across sources.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.summary: Land any 250 of the game's 397 stunts, mixed freely across stunt jumps, under-bridge flights, knife flights and base jumps [1].
steps: Know the pool: 130 stunt jumps, 202 under-the-bridge flights, 40 knife flights and 25 base jumps make 397 stunts in total [1].
Start with under-bridge flights — the guide rates them the quickest category to bank in bulk [1].
Track progress by region under Progress, then Activities, then Stunts, and cross-check named spots on the map under Exploration, then Stunt Spots [1].
Remember the trophy needs 250 but the 100% checklist needs 300, so keep going past the trophy if you are on the platinum route [1][8].
Use the counter on this row to log stunts as you clear each region rather than guessing later [1].
Bank the under-bridge flights in batches; they are the fastest category and they carry the count while you travel [1].

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.summary: Sample all 9 activity types the tracker counts — fishing, hunting, golf, shooting ranges, pool, basketball, a video game, a race and a stunt among them [1].
steps: Open the tracker view of your progress: Touchpad, then Progress, then Activities shows each type and how many you have done [1].
Work the named types once each: fishing, hunting, golf, shooting ranges, pool, basketball hoops, a video game, a car or drone race, and a stunt [1].
Most types are introduced by the story itself; the rest appear as blue activity icons when you unfog the map [1].
Filter the map for Activities (the blue dumbbell icon) to find any type you are missing [1].
Expect this to complete almost by itself while you work the other trophies and the 100% checklist [1][8].
One type is easy to forget: a video game at home counts, and it doubles as progress toward Stick Fiddler [1].

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.summary: Gold-medal every shooting range challenge: 42 golds spread across the range locations, and the full set is also required by the 100% checklist [1].

Play each challenge once to learn its targets and scoring before chasing gold [1].
Raise your Focus stat as you go; range challenges are one of the activities the guide names for building Focus, which makes later golds easier [1].
Re-run any challenge that lands silver until it turns gold, and log each gold on this row's counter [1].
Finish all 42: unlike most categories, the 100% checklist wants every range done too, so no gold here is wasted [1][8].
Range golds also grow your Focus, which returns the favour at the Gunslinger feat later in the run [1].

Fly a grid over the state, region by region, watching the map fill in [1].
Mop up coastal and island edges last, where thin fog strips are easy to miss [1].
When no fog remains anywhere, the trophy unlocks [1][2].

Fund it with robberies as your income grows through Chapters 3 and 4 [1].
